Stage1.name: Incubation
Stage1.desc: Back the project. Your deposit sits in escrow and can be withdrawn at cost at any time.
Stage1.whatNow: Deposit, test the product, leave signed feedback. Nothing is at risk yet.
Stage1.path: 15–60 days · exit at cost any time

Stage2.name: Series A buffer
Stage2.desc: A dampened-curve pool is open. Outside buyers set the price, which converges to the Uniswap price by the end of the stage. Backers can still exit at cost.
Stage2.whatNow: Exit at cost at any time, or realise profit along the curve. Tokens stay in the protocol ledger until listing.

Stage3.name: Open market
Stage3.desc: Listed on Uniswap. Ordinary market risk from here.
Stage3.whatNow: Trade on Uniswap, or keep your tokens where they are and receive the Diamond Hand stream.

Dissolved.name: Dissolved
Dissolved.desc: The project did not graduate and was dissolved. Every backer takes back their full principal at cost, or moves it into another project.
Dissolved.whatNow: Take back your full principal, or move it into another project in one transaction.

home.title: Back cutting-edge AI innovation, as an early VC with protective terms.
home.sub: In an era where AI is reshaping everything, every startup needs the room to experiment. Portex is the first escrow-backed on-chain incubation protocol: funds remain fully protected until genuine external demand is proven. If a project does not graduate from incubation, backers can reclaim 100% of their principal with zero loss; only when a project truly breaks out does it enter the open market.
home.kpiFormula: Protected = total escrow; live = Stage 1 and Stage 2 including pending listing; graduated = Stage 3. Backers are summed per launch.
home.boundary: Cost exits end when the open market begins; on Budget Launches, a voted budget can reduce principal. Without external demand, there is no loss and no profit, subject to that budget boundary.
home.allocationNote: Diamond Hand is an allocation mechanism: a defined token allocation and fee revenue are distributed according to eligibility. Amounts depend on activity; returns are never promised.

protection.title: Protected until demand is proven.
protection.desc: Funds stay in on-chain escrow through Stage 1 and Stage 2. Until genuine external demand arrives, backers may reclaim 100% of their principal at any time, with zero fees, or move it into another project in one transaction.

founders.title: Founders on the same terms as you.
founders.desc: No free tokens. Founders buy in along the same gentle curve and vest for three years after listing. The last backer pays at most 1.5× the first.

spending.title: Spending only by vote.
spending.desc: All fees go to a treasury that pays out only through proposals and votes: by contributed capital before listing, by token holders after. In an Escrow Launch the team never touches the raise.

allocation.title: Rewards for those who stay.
allocation.desc: 30% of supply, plus fee revenue, streams daily for three years to wallets that never moved their tokens.

protocol.title: Protocol
protocol.description: Every raise uses an immutable, published template version. Inspect the code, verify its hashes and see who can act before depositing.

guarantees.title: The base layer: what every launch includes

exit.d: Every launch begins with incubation. Each position can be exited at its exact cost, with zero fees, until the listing transaction executes. On Budget Launches an executed budget reduces every claim proportionally.

custody.d: On an Escrow Launch no function lets the team withdraw the raise. On a Budget Launch the only path is a capped draw that backers vote through.

pinned.d: The template version, price curve, schedule and treasury are pinned when the launch is created and cannot change afterwards.

liquidity.d: Liquidity added to Uniswap at listing is owned by the launch contract and can never be withdrawn; only its trading fees are collected, to the treasury.

analyst.d: The AI analyst may delay Stage 1 within a fixed budget. It can never approve a launch or move funds.

guarantees.sub: These rules belong to the protocol itself. A template may tune parameters such as thresholds and caps, but no template can remove them.

treasury.d: Every fee goes to the launch's own treasury, together with 10% of supply that unlocks over five years after listing. Each spend is a proposal and a vote: by contributed capital before listing, by token holders after.

dissolution.d: A project that does not graduate is dissolved and every position claims its full cost. After the Stage 1 minimum, the team may also dissolve it early and return later with a new version.

rollover.t: Move between projects in one transaction
rollover.d: Positions in projects that have not listed, and dissolution claims, move straight into another project's Stage 1. No withdrawal in between, one transaction, one fee.

founders.t: Founders buy on the same terms
founders.d: There is no free allocation. Team purchases follow the public curve, are capped at 10% of supply, and vest for three years after a one-month cliff.

metadata.description: Principal-protected launches for AI projects on X Layer. Whatever is still in escrow is yours 1:1 — you take risk only on what you opt in.

sealed.name: ESCROW
sealed.title: Escrow Launch
sealed.definition: The team never touches the raise. It is funded by treasury budgets that pass a vote, from trading fees and a 10% token allocation, and by its own revenue.
sealed.builderGets: Treasury budgets approved by vote: trading fees and the 10% treasury allocation, which unlocks over five years after listing. Plus the project's own revenue. Never the raise.
sealed.suitedTo: Software and tools with their own business model, sustained by revenue and fees.
sealed.empty: No launches of this type match the selected stage.
sealed.boundary: Cost exits end when the open market begins. The team cannot spend the raise.

milestone.builderGets: Budgets from the raise approved by backers within the disclosed cap; after listing, voted treasury budgets. Plus the project's own revenue.
milestone.suitedTo: Compute-heavy teams that need structured capital.
milestone.empty: No launches of this type match the selected stage.
milestone.boundary: Cost exits end when the open market begins. A voted budget can reduce principal.

docs.title: Docs
docs.description: How Portex works and how to use it: step-by-step guides for backers, builders, traders, analysts and administrators, the three stages, what protects your principal and where it ends, the governed treasury, fees, trading after listing, and the deployed contracts.

Stage1.what: Back the project at the curve price. Exit at cost at any time, with zero fees.

Stage2.what: Outside buyers set the price. Exit at cost, or with protected profit funded by their demand.

Stage3.what: The project trades on Uniswap v4. Protection has ended; ordinary market risk applies.

stepper.dissolution: A project that does not graduate from Stage 1 is dissolved, and every position claims its full cost.
stepper.note: Lengths are production defaults. Where this network pins shorter timings, they appear under each stage.

overview.title: Portex in one page
overview.lede: An on-chain incubation protocol for AI startups on X Layer, in the founder's own words:
overview.p1: Portex holds every deposit in escrow under rules fixed before the first deposit. A project reaches the open market only after two stages that test for **genuine external demand**, and until then every backer can leave at exactly what they paid.
overview.p2: A launchpad sells tokens and steps aside. Portex stays in the middle: it custodies the raise, prices it on a published curve, keeps each backer's cost claim alive until listing, and lists the project on Uniswap v4 with liquidity that can never be withdrawn.
pillars: **Protected until demand is proven.** In Stage 1 and Stage 2, any backer can exit at their exact cost, with zero fees, or move it into another project in one transaction.
**Founders on the same terms.** No free tokens. Team purchases follow the same curve, are capped at 10% of supply and vest for three years after listing.
**Spending only by vote.** All fees and 10% of the token supply go to the project's own treasury, which pays out only through proposals that pass a vote.
**Rewards for those who stay.** 30% of supply, plus a share of Stage 2 fees, streams daily for three years to original backers who keep their tokens.

lifecycle.title: The lifecycle
lifecycle.lede: Every launch, of either type, runs through the same three stages. Each stage has a deadline, and anyone can move the launch forward when it is due.
lifecycle.p1: Protection is a property of the stage, not a promise about the project. Until the listing transaction executes, every backer position can be exited at its exact cost; on a Budget Launch, that is its cost after any voted budgets. Listing ends this claim for everyone at once and delivers the tokens as ordinary ERC-20 balances.
lifecycle.p2: The builder chooses both stage lengths within bounds set by the protocol, and they are fixed before the first deposit. See [Governed timings](#timings).

stage1.lede: The project raises its first capital at a price set by a published curve, while every deposit waits in escrow.
canList: **Deposit** USDG. You receive tokens at the curve price, which rises linearly with every token sold, so the last backer pays at most 1.5× what the first paid. Up to 20% of the supply is sold in this stage.
**Exit at cost** at any time, in part or in full: you get back exactly what you paid for the tokens you return.
**Move** your position into another project's Stage 1 in one transaction. See [Rollover](#dissolution-rollover).
**Review** the project: the builder's updates, the AI analyst's report and signed feedback from other backers.
stage1.protectsNote: Your deposit stays in escrow, apart from every other balance. Nothing can be spent in Stage 1: no fees, no budgets and no token transfers. Your tokens are a ledger entry held by the protocol, so no one can open a pool before listing.
endsList: **Graduation** to Stage 2 at the deadline, if backers still hold at least 95% of the Stage 1 allocation and at least 10 backers other than the builder hold positions. Selling the whole allocation takes the price to the project's own target valuation (at least $100,000).
**Dissolution** otherwise, or earlier if the builder dissolves the project after the Stage 1 minimum. Every position then claims its full cost. See [Dissolution](#dissolution).
The AI analyst may **delay** graduation within a fixed budget, but cannot prevent it. See [The AI analyst](#analyst).

stage2.lede: Outside buyers can now trade against the protocol's book. The price starts at the final Stage 1 price and converges gradually on the price the project will list at.
canList: **Exit at cost** at any time until listing, exactly as in Stage 1.
**Take a protected exit**: your cost plus the elapsed share of your gain, paid only from real outside demand. See [Exits](#exits).
**Vote** on budget and treasury proposals with your contributed capital. See [Treasury and voting](#treasury).
Outside buyers **buy and sell** in the book with a 1% fee. Their tokens stay in a ledger until listing and have no cost protection.
stage2.priceText: The book pairs real USDG from outside buyers with virtual depth that shrinks linearly over the stage. At the first moment the price is exactly the final Stage 1 price; at the last, exactly the price the pool will open at. In between it converges gradually, so a burst of speculation cannot run far ahead of real demand.
stage2.protectsNote: Your cost stays in escrow and can be taken back at any time. Profit is never paid from other backers' principal: it comes only from the reserve that outside buyers funded. Without outside demand, there is no profit and no loss. On a Budget Launch, a budget that backers approved by vote can reduce your cost.
stage2.endsText: Listing is mandatory at the Stage 2 deadline, whatever the demand. Anyone can execute it. If the call to the venue fails, the whole transaction reverts: cost exits stay open, and anyone can try again.

stage3.lede: The project lists on Uniswap v4. Protection ends, and ordinary market risk begins.
listingList: The remaining escrow and the book's reserve become liquidity in a 1% Uniswap v4 pool, opened at the book's final price. The protocol locks this liquidity permanently; only its fees are collected, to the project treasury.
Every backer and buyer receives their tokens as ordinary ERC-20 balances, automatically. There is nothing to claim.
Team purchases move into vesting: a 30-day cliff, then linear release over three years.
The 10% treasury allocation arrives in the project's treasury and starts to unlock.
canList: **Trade** on the [Markets](/markets) page, or through any Uniswap v4 interface.
**Hold** and receive the Diamond Hand stream: 30% of the supply, plus the rewards share of Stage 2 fees, released daily over three years to original backers in proportion to their reward quota.
**Vote** on treasury proposals with your tokens.
stage3.quotaNote: Reward quota belongs to original backers' tokens. Any transfer or sale destroys the same amount of quota, and it never returns. Stage 2 buyers and team purchases carry no quota. Diamond Hand is an allocation, not a yield: amounts depend on activity and are never promised.

launchTypes.title: Launch types
launchTypes.lede: Both types share the same stages, protections, treasury rules and fees. They differ in one thing: whether a voted budget may draw on the raise before listing.

head: Escrow Launch
Budget Launch
rows: Draws on the raise
None. The team never touches the raise.
Only by backers' vote, within a cap disclosed before the first deposit: at most 30% of the escrow at the start of Stage 2.
Size of each draw
At most 10% of the capital voting YES. Every position's cost is reduced in proportion.
What an exit at cost returns
Your original cost
Your cost after any voted draws
Builder income
Treasury budgets that pass a vote (fees and the 10% token allocation), and the project's own revenue
Voted draws on the raise before listing; afterwards, treasury budgets that pass a vote; and the project's own revenue
Suited to
Software and tools with their own business model
Compute-heavy teams that need structured capital before listing

launchTypes.escrowText: The contract gives the builder no path to backers' funds. The team is paid the way a project on its own feet is paid: from the treasury, whose income is trading fees and a 10% token allocation that unlocks over five years{{treasuryVesting}}, spent only by proposals that pass a vote; and from the product's own revenue.
launchTypes.budgetText: For teams that need capital before listing. The builder chooses a budget ceiling when creating the launch, and it is shown before anyone deposits. In Stage 2 each draw is a proposal that backers vote on with their capital; a draw that passes reduces every position's cost in proportion. Backers can still exit at cost during the vote and the dispute window, so no one is carried into a budget they reject.

exits.title: Exits
exits.lede: Until listing, a backer can always leave. There are two ways out.
exits.costText: Available in Stage 1, in Stage 2 and while listing is pending, for any part of a position. You receive exactly the cost of the tokens you return (your cost × tokens returned ÷ tokens held), with zero fees. In Stage 1 those tokens go back on sale for other backers; after Stage 1 they are burned. Votes, AI delays and failed listing attempts never block it.
exits.protectedText: Backers can also leave with profit. The payout is your cost plus the elapsed share of your gain: if the book values your tokens above your cost, you receive that gain multiplied by the share of Stage 2 that has passed. Early in the stage you receive about your cost; near the end, about the full market value.
exits.protectedSource: The profit is paid only from the real reserve that outside buyers funded, never from other backers' escrow. The book keeps only as many of your tokens as it needs to fund the profit; the rest are burned. Without outside demand, the profit is zero and you receive your cost.
exits.example: Example: you paid 1,000 USDG. Halfway through Stage 2, the book would pay 1,400 USDG for your tokens. A protected exit pays up to 1,000 + 50% × 400 = 1,200 USDG, as far as the real reserve can fund it.
exits.buyers: Stage 2 buyers are not backers: they sell back to the book at its price, with the 1% fee, and have no cost protection. Team purchases can exit at cost but take no profit.

dissolution.title: Dissolution and rollover
dissolution.lede: A project that does not graduate is dissolved, and every position takes back its full cost.
dissolutionList: At the Stage 1 deadline, a project that has not met its gates is dissolved automatically.
After the Stage 1 minimum, the builder may dissolve the project early.
Every position then claims its exact remaining cost from the project's claim vault, at any time, with no deadline. An unclaimed position never blocks anyone else's claim.
dissolution.dissolutionText: Dissolution is a normal outcome of incubation. It ends the raise; it does not reduce anyone's claim.
dissolution.rolloverText: Capital can move between projects in one transaction. The rollover router exits your positions in projects that have not listed (at cost, or with protected profit in Stage 2) and takes your dissolution claims, adds an optional top-up from your wallet, deposits the total into another project's Stage 1 in your name, and returns anything unused.

fees.title: Fees
fees.lede: Portex charges no protocol fee. Every fee a launch collects stays with that launch.

head: When
Fee
Where it goes
rows: Stage 1 deposits and exits
None
Stage 2 buys and sells by outside buyers
1% of each trade
40% stays in the book's reserve, 30% to the Diamond Hand rewards, 30% to the project treasury
Exits at cost and protected exits
None
Swaps in the Portex pool after listing
1% Uniswap v4 pool fee
The fees on the protocol's locked liquidity go to the project treasury
Rollover and dissolution claims
None

fees.p1: The reserve share deepens the book that funds protected exits. The reward and treasury shares are held in separate buckets and never mix with principal.

treasury.title: Treasury and voting
treasury.lede: Every launch has its own treasury, created with it. Nothing leaves it without a proposal that passes a vote.
sourcesList: The treasury share of Stage 2 trading fees.
Fees earned by the protocol's locked liquidity after listing.
Reward funds that can no longer be distributed.
10% of the token supply, which arrives at listing and unlocks on a straight line over five years (the production default){{treasuryVesting}}. Locked tokens can never be spent.
treasury.capitalText: In Stage 2, proposals are voted by contributed capital, never by tokens: each backer position votes once, weighted by its cost. A proposal needs a quorum of 40% of eligible capital and 60% approval, and may spend at most 10% of the capital voting YES. Voting lasts three days{{voting}}; a passed proposal then waits through a seven-day dispute window{{dispute}}, during which any backer can still exit at cost, and can be executed within the next two days{{execution}}. Exiting cancels that position's vote. One proposal runs at a time, and each new proposal comes at least one day after the previous one was made{{proposalInterval}}.
treasury.tokensText: In Stage 3, token holders vote with their balance at the end of the block in which the proposal was made, so borrowed tokens cannot sway it. A proposal passes with 60% of the votes cast, and its total value may not exceed 5% of the market value of the tokens voting YES, valued at the lower of the listing price and the current pool price. The builder's addresses cannot vote.
treasury.teamText: An Escrow Launch team is paid by treasury budgets that pass a vote and by the product's own revenue. A Budget Launch team can also draw on the raise, by vote and within its cap, before listing. Neither receives free tokens.

analyst.title: The AI analyst
analyst.lede: Every raise in Stage 1 is reviewed by an AI analyst that publishes a risk report on the project page. It has one power: it can delay.
list: It may place a veto that delays graduation from Stage 1: at most two days per veto{{vetoMax}} and seven days in total{{vetoTotal}}, with a one-day cooldown between vetoes{{vetoCooldown}}, and never beyond the Stage 1 maximum.
It cannot approve a launch, reject one that met its gates, or touch any funds.
Cost exits stay open during a delay.
The council can lift a veto early. The delay budget already used is not restored.
The builder can respond publicly to every report.

roles.title: Roles and their limits
roles.lede: A few addresses have narrow roles, pinned into every launch. None can change a live launch or move backers' funds.

head: Role
Can
Cannot
rows: Curator
Publish new template versions, deprecate versions for new launches, whitelist the quote asset, and set governed parameters for future versions
Change a published version or an existing launch; touch funds
Attester
Post the AI analyst's veto, within the delay budget
Approve or reject a launch; touch funds
Council
Lift an active veto early
Extend a veto or restore its budget; touch funds
Builder
Create a launch, post updates, propose budgets and treasury spends, and dissolve the project after the Stage 1 minimum
Receive free tokens, buy more than 10% of the supply, vote on proposals, or spend without a vote
Anyone
Advance a stage when it is due, execute the listing, and finalize or execute proposals
API administrator (off-chain)
Run the AI analyst on demand, without the rate limit
Anything on-chain

roles.p1: Each launch pins its code, parameters, quote asset and roles when it is created. No one, including the curator, can upgrade a live launch.

timings.title: Governed timings
timings.lede: Stage lengths and governance windows are protocol parameters. The curator sets them for future versions only; each version pins its values, and every launch keeps the values of its version.
timings.p1: The table compares the production defaults with the values a new launch on this network pins today, read live from the current template version.
timings.p2: The builder picks each launch's stage lengths within these bounds, and they are fixed before the first deposit. On testnet the timings are shortened so a whole lifecycle can be seen in a day; the contracts are identical, and only the governed parameters differ. Production launches use the production defaults.

markets.title: Markets and trading
markets.lede: After listing, each project trades in its own Uniswap v4 pool.
list: The [Markets](/markets) page lists every project in Stage 3 · Open market with its price, 24-hour change and volume, pool liquidity and FDV (price × total supply).
Each project's trading page shows its whole price history in candles from one minute to one day: the Stage 2 book, the listing moment and the pool.

Swaps are exact-input and go through the Portex swap router in one transaction. The panel shows a live quote from the pool, the price impact, the pool fee and the minimum you will receive under your slippage tolerance (1% by default). If the price moves beyond it before your transaction confirms, nothing is exchanged.
Your first trade of each asset asks you to approve the router.
Selling tokens that carry reward quota destroys the same amount of quota.
The pool is an ordinary Uniswap v4 pool, so other interfaces can trade it too. Its listing liquidity is locked permanently.

testnet.title: Connect to X Layer testnet
testnet.lede: Portex runs on X Layer testnet with a test quote asset. Your wallet needs this network and a little test OKB for gas.
list: When you press **Connect wallet**, the app asks your wallet to switch to X Layer testnet, and to add it if it is missing. You can also add it by hand with the values above.
Get test OKB for gas from the [OKX X Layer faucet](https://web3.okx.com/xlayer/faucet).

**TEST USDG** is a freely mintable faucet token with 6 decimals, like USDG. It has no monetary value and is never real USDG. When your balance is empty, the deposit and trade panels, and an empty Portfolio, offer to mint 10,000 TEST USDG in one transaction.
Testnet launches can use shortened timings, so a project can go from Stage 1 to the open market in less than an hour. See [Governed timings](#timings).

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.lede: Short answers; each links to the section with the details.

items.a: Not before listing on an Escrow Launch: you can exit at your exact cost at any time until the listing transaction. On a Budget Launch, a draw that backers approved by vote reduces every position's cost in proportion. After listing, your tokens carry ordinary market risk. See [Exits](#exits).

items.q: What happens if nobody buys in Stage 2?
items.a: The project still lists at the end of Stage 2. Without outside demand there is no profit: a protected exit pays your cost, and at listing your tokens become tradable at the book's final price.

items.q: Why can't I transfer my tokens before listing?
items.a: No one can, so no one can open a pool early and graduate a project around the protocol. Until listing, backers can exit at cost and Stage 2 buyers can sell back to the book.

items.q: Who decides when a project lists?
items.a: The calendar. Listing is due at the Stage 2 deadline chosen before the first deposit, and anyone can execute it.

items.q: Can the team take the money and leave?
items.a: On an Escrow Launch, the contract gives the team no path to the raise. On a Budget Launch, only draws that backers approved by vote, within the disclosed cap. Treasury funds move only through proposals that pass a vote.

items.q: Does the AI decide which projects succeed?
items.a: No. The analyst can only delay Stage 1 within a fixed budget. It cannot approve, reject or touch funds. See [The AI analyst](#analyst).

items.q: Are Diamond Hand rewards a yield?
items.a: No. They are an allocation of tokens and fee revenue that streams to original backers who keep their tokens. Amounts depend on activity and are never promised.
To the launch itself: its reserve, its rewards and its treasury. Portex charges no protocol fee. See [Fees](#fees).
Fully diluted value: the current price multiplied by the total token supply.

items.q: Can a launch be changed after I deposit?
items.a: No. Its code, parameters and roles are pinned when it is created. New versions apply only to new launches.

items.q: Where can I check the contracts?
items.a: Every address is listed in [Deployed contracts](#contracts), with a link to the block explorer.

glossary.title: Glossary
glossary.lede: The terms used across Portex, in plain words.

items.def: Anyone who deposited in Stage 1. A backer position has a cost that can be exited until listing.
The protocol's market in Stage 2: real USDG from outside buyers plus virtual depth that shrinks over the stage.
The team that created the launch.
What a position paid for its remaining tokens; on a Budget Launch, after any voted draws.
The reward stream for original backers who keep their tokens: 30% of supply plus the rewards share of Stage 2 fees, released daily over three years.
The end of a project that does not graduate from Stage 1. Every position claims its full cost.
Where deposits wait until listing, apart from every other balance.
Leaving a position and receiving exactly its cost, with zero fees.
Fully diluted value: price × total supply.
The transaction that ends Stage 2: it opens the Uniswap v4 pool, locks its liquidity and delivers every token.
A Stage 2 exit that pays your cost plus the elapsed share of your gain, funded only by outside demand.
The share of eligible capital that must vote for a Stage 2 proposal to count: 40%.
The part of an original backer's tokens that earns Diamond Hand rewards. Transfers and sales destroy it.
Moving positions and dissolution claims into another project's Stage 1 in one transaction.
How far below the quoted amount a swap may settle before it is cancelled.
A freely mintable test token on X Layer testnet, with no monetary value.
A launch's own vault for its fees and its 10% token allocation. It pays only through proposals that pass a vote.
A delay the AI analyst may place on graduation from Stage 1, within a fixed budget.
The fingerprint of a template version: its implementations, parameters and roles. Every launch records the one it was created with; see [Deployed contracts](#contracts).

guideBacker.title: Backer guide
guideBacker.lede: From your first deposit to listing, or to taking your principal back.
joinSteps: Open **Projects** and choose a project in **Stage 1 · Incubation**. Its page shows the stage and the time left, and the **Overview** tab holds the description, the AI analyst's report and the builder's updates.
Press **Connect wallet**. On testnet, if your USDG balance is empty, the deposit panel offers to mint TEST USDG; you also need a little test OKB for gas. See [Connect to X Layer testnet](#testnet).
In **What you can do now**, choose **Deposit** and enter an amount. The quote shows the tokens you receive and what you pay; any amount the curve cannot use is returned.

The first time, the button reads **Approve USDG**: approve, then press **Deposit** and confirm in the transaction drawer. To pay with capital from another project, set **Pay from** to **Other projects**.
leaveSteps: Choose **Exit at cost**, pick the position and the quantity. You receive exactly what those tokens cost, with zero fees, at any time until the listing transaction.
In Stage 2, **Protected exit** pays your cost plus the elapsed share of your gain, as far as outside demand has funded it. The quote shows the cost and the profit separately.
Under **Treasury & votes**, vote on budgets and treasury spends with **Vote YES** or **Vote NO**. Voting never blocks an exit.
afterSteps: When Stage 2 ends, anyone can press **List on Uniswap**. Your tokens then arrive in your wallet automatically; there is nothing to claim.
Keep your tokens to receive the Diamond Hand stream, and press **Claim rewards** on the project page. Selling or transferring reduces your reward quota.
If the project is dissolved instead, press **Take back principal**, or **Move into another project** to deposit it straight into another Stage 1.
**Portfolio** lists every position, and the bell in the header shows what needs you: claims, votes and listings.

guideBuilder.title: Builder guide
guideBuilder.lede: Launching a project, running it through the stages, and what you receive.
launchSteps: Choose the launch type. **Escrow Launch** if the product can fund itself from treasury budgets and its own revenue; **Budget Launch** if you need voted draws on the raise before listing. See [Launch types](#launchTypes).

Open **Launch a project** and work through the steps: **Launch type**, **Basics** (name, symbol, description, website), **Capital** (supply and target valuation, at least $100,000), **Schedule** (the two stage lengths, within the bounds shown), **Rules** (additional builder addresses and, for a Budget Launch, the budget ceiling) and **Review**.
Press **Launch project** and sign. The terms are fixed from this moment and cannot be changed after anyone deposits.
runSteps: On your project page, press **Open builder console**. Fill in the **Project profile**, choose **Upload image** for the **Project image** (PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to 2 MB), then **Sign & save profile**.
Use **Post a public update** for milestones and incidents; backers read them on the project page.
When the analyst publishes a report, answer it under **Respond to the latest analyst report**. Your response appears beside the report.
You may buy on the same curve as everyone else, up to 10% of the supply in total. Your purchases do not count toward the minimum of 10 backers and carry no reward quota.

Budget Launch, Stage 2: under **Treasury & votes**, **Propose a draw**. Backers vote by capital. When voting ends, anyone can **Finalize vote**; once the dispute window has passed, **Execute budget** pays the draw and reduces every position's cost in proportion.
endSteps: At the Stage 2 deadline anyone lists the project. Your purchases then vest: a 30-day cliff, then linear release over three years; press **Claim vested tokens** as they unlock.
After listing, fund the work with **Propose a treasury spend**. Token holders vote; your own addresses cannot.
If the project should not continue, **Dissolve project** once the Stage 1 minimum has passed. Every position then takes back its full cost.

guideTrader.title: Trader guide
guideTrader.lede: Buying and selling before listing in the Stage 2 book, and after listing in the pool.
bookSteps: Open a project in **Stage 2 · Series A buffer**. The **Market** tab shows the price chart and the recent trades.
In **What you can do now**, choose **Buy**, enter USDG and set the price tolerance. The quote shows the tokens you receive, the 1% trading fee, the price impact and the minimum you will accept.
Your tokens stay in the protocol's ledger until listing. You can **Sell** them back to the book at any time until then, again with a 1% fee. At listing they arrive in your wallet.
poolSteps: Open **Markets** and choose a project. The page shows the price in candles, the recent trades and the pool's facts.

In the trade panel, choose **Buy** or **Sell** and enter the amount you pay. The quote comes live from the pool: average price, price impact, the 1% pool fee and the minimum received under your slippage tolerance (1% by default).
The first trade of each asset asks you to approve the Portex swap router; then confirm the swap in the transaction drawer. If the price moves beyond your tolerance first, nothing is exchanged.
risksList: Stage 2 buyers are not backers: they have no cost protection, no protected exit and no reward quota.
After listing, the price is set by an open market and can fall below what anyone paid.
Large trades move the price. Check the price impact against the pool's liquidity.
Selling tokens that carry reward quota destroys the same amount of quota.

guideAnalyst.title: Analyst guide
guideAnalyst.lede: What the AI analyst does, and how people and programs can read the same data.
aiList: It reviews each raise in Stage 1, including the number of backers and the share of capital linked to the builder, and publishes a report with a risk score and findings on the project's **Overview** tab.
It may delay graduation from Stage 1 with a veto, within a fixed budget. It cannot approve, reject or touch funds. See [The AI analyst](#analyst).
The builder can answer every report publicly.
guideAnalyst.apiText: Everything in the app is also available as JSON, without an account or a key. The testnet API is at `https://testnet-api.portex.vc/v2`. Amounts are integers in base units (USDG has 6 decimals, tokens 18) and prices are scaled by 10^18, except on the market endpoints (`/markets`, `candles`, `pool-trades`), which return decimal strings in USDG per token.

head: Endpoint
Returns
rows: `GET /raises`
Every raise with its stage, prices and key figures; add `?phase=Stage1` to filter by stage.
`GET /raises/{address}`
One raise in full: configuration, book, treasury, listing record and the latest report.
`GET /raises/{address}/trades`
Stage 1 and Stage 2 activity in the protocol's ledger: deposits, exits, buys and sells.
`GET /raises/{address}/candles?interval=1h`
Price candles of the Stage 2 book and the pool, from `1m` to `1d`.
`GET /raises/{address}/pool-trades`
Swaps in the Uniswap v4 pool after listing, with the trader.
`GET /raises/{address}/activity`
A readable feed of the raise's on-chain events.
`GET /raises/{address}/proposals`
Budget and treasury proposals with their votes, caps and state.
`GET /raises/{address}/reports`
The AI analyst's reports and the builder's responses.
`GET /markets`
Every project in Stage 3 · Open market: price, 24-hour change and volume, liquidity and FDV.
`GET /config`
Deployed addresses, the quote asset and the parameters each template version pins.

guideAnalyst.apiNote: Every value can be checked against the contracts in [Deployed contracts](#contracts). Writes to the chain always go through your own wallet, never through the API.

guideAdmin.title: Administrator guide
guideAdmin.lede: The protocol's roles, what the Admin console lets each one do, and where their power ends.
guideAdmin.p1: The **Admin** item appears in the navigation only when the connected wallet holds a role. The console shows each role's actions and says why an action is unavailable.
curatorSteps: **Protocol parameters**: **Edit parameters**, review the changes, then **Set protocol parameters**. The values apply only to the next published version.

**Template versions**: **Publish** the next version, which pins the current implementations and parameters; **Deprecate** a version so new launches can no longer use it. Existing launches keep theirs.
**Quote asset**: **Whitelist a quote asset** for versions published afterwards.
attesterSteps: **Vetoes** lists every raise in Stage 1 with its latest report, its veto budget and its cooldown.
Enter a delay and **Apply veto**. A veto cites the latest report, lasts at most the per-veto maximum and must fit in the remaining budget.
councilSteps: Under **Vetoes**, **Clear veto** lifts an active veto early. The budget already used is not restored.
limitsList: Parameters, versions and quote admission affect future launches only. No role can change a live launch.
No role can move backers' funds, block an exit or spend from a treasury.
A veto only delays graduation; it cannot reject a project that met its gates.
API administrators can run the analyst on demand without the rate limit (**Analysis**, **Run analysis now**). This is an off-chain role.

contracts.title: Deployed contracts
contracts.lede: Every contract this app uses on the current network, read from the deployment record. Copy an address, or open it in the block explorer.
contracts.p1: The implementations are the code every new launch is cloned from; each launch pins them, with its parameters, through the bundle hash of its template version.
contracts.p2: Pools run on a Uniswap v4 PoolManager deployed from the unmodified v4.0.0 release. Liquidity added at listing is owned by each raise through the adapter and can never be withdrawn.
